local_validation_commands: GOWORK=off go run ./cmd/unified_bench -dbs treedb,treedb_public_command_wal -test batch_write -keys 200000 -batchsize 1024 -valsize 32 -profile wal_on_fast -treedb-maintenance-mode bench -treedb-command-wal-stats-scan -progress=false -format markdown

performance_gate.rationale: Public command-WAL writes use the cached write path instead of direct backend root publication per point Set, preserve public batch fast paths, stream RawKVBatch payload encoding directly from replayable batches in one hinted pass, avoid one-shot public Set/Delete slice plus backend intent allocations, and append point-write command frames without a separate payload allocation or buffered-writer flush layer. Benchmark artifacts include explicit command_wal_cached mode proof. Longer Batch.Write focused runs remain below parity for batch size 64 by roughly 12% and batch size 1024 by roughly 18%; the end-to-end unified_bench public cached batch_write lane remains roughly 24% below legacy cached throughput in this run. Point Set allocation parity is preserved and throughput is improved relative to the initial PR9 path, but it remains materially slower because every public Set still appends and flushes a typed command-WAL frame. This gate is improved performance evidence but not a passed strict parity gate; default cutover should remain blocked unless an explicit threshold/follow-up is accepted.

unsupported_modes: Update/UpdateSync remain rejected under cached public command-WAL until they have typed command coverage
DeleteRange remains rejected under cached public command-WAL until it has typed command coverage
next_required_work: decide whether point Set command-frame append/flush cost is acceptable only under an explicit threshold, or keep PR9 default cutover blocked
optimize public command-WAL batch_write enough for consistent batch size 1024 and unified_bench parity, or record an explicit accepted threshold and follow-up issue before default enablement
